_comment: SHA-256 pins for the ffmpeg/ffprobe sidecars fetched by scripts/fetch-ffmpeg.mjs, keyed by <name>-<rust host triple>. This is the SECOND pin layer: the script already hard-pins the SHA-256 of every downloaded ARCHIVE, so these cover the exact unpacked bytes that get bundled and shipped. A mismatch hard-fails the fetch; a MISSING key only warns (see checkPin) — which is safe only because the archive pin above it never can be missing, so never delete a key here expecting the fetch to stop. Reset for ffmpeg 9.0.1 (2026-09-19, was 8.1.2). All three shipping/CI hosts were pinned up front on the owner's machine this time, not from CI logs: mac arm64 by running the fetch script itself, windows + linux by extracting the same members from archives first verified against the publishers' .sha256 files (the Windows CI lane never downloads the real binary, so a CI-log pin would only have arrived with the first release). An x86_64-apple-darwin entry is still absent because no Intel mac build exists yet; add one when the universal build lands.
